title: Ethnoecology as Deep History
description: Explores the deep history of sustainability, resilience and collapse in past societies. Examines how communities across cultures and throughout time managed ecosystems, food systems and urbanization, and how inequality and governance shaped resilience or vulnerability. Archaeological case studies highlight both fragility and innovation, offering lessons for today’s challenges in food security, biodiversity, governance and climate adaptation.
notes: Credit will be granted for only one of ES 434, ES 481 (if taken in the same topic).
